items.title: Forget Being a Landlord: These 3 REITs Pay You to Own Apartments
items.summary: Apartment REITs are legally required to hand most of their income straight to shareholders, but not all of them are equally safe bets right now. Three landlords are collecting rent checks while new construction dries up, and the differences between them could cost you real money.

items.title: Meet Wall Street’s Dependable High-Yield Dividend Stocks: 4 Companies Still Raising Their Payouts Year After Year
items.summary: Tax law forces REITs to hand over most of their income, leaving almost no cushion for mistakes. So which landlords keep lifting payouts anyway, and what separates the safe raisers from the ones quietly stretching their cash?

items.title: Buy and Hold Forever: 4 Dividend Stocks That Pay You More Every Year
items.summary: Tax law forces REITs to hand over nearly all their income, so a rising payout needs real cash growth behind it. Four equity REITs pass the test, but one has a thin cushion that could keep its raises small.

items.title: Sitting on a $1.22 Million 401(k)? The Roth Conversion Math That Turns Future RMDs Into $5,592 a Month Tax-Free
items.summary: The IRS will force money out of a big 401(k) on its own schedule and tax every dollar as ordinary income. A few low-income years before age 75 give you a narrow window to change that, but one early move could raise your Medicare bill.
